findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key you were issued. Append it as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Passing the API key as a query parameter returns 401 Unauthorized with 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. All requests must supply the key in the X-API-Key HTTP header.
findings.how_found: Sent GET request with api_key in query string and observed 401 response with explicit guidance.
findings.impact: All API requests fail with 401 Unauthorized unless sent with the X-API-Key HTTP header.
evidence: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-A3B2763F67F9 -> HTTP 401: send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter

findings.documented: Tokens are valid for 24 hours. There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Tokens expire in 15 minutes (900s) and a refresh flow exists via POST /auth/refresh. Returns access_token instead of token, and user object omits name.
findings.how_found: Inspected POST /auth/login response payload and tested /auth/refresh with returned refresh_token.
findings.impact: Frontend sessions expire prematurely after 15 minutes without implementing the undocumented refresh flow.
evidence: POST /auth/login -> HTTP 200: { access_token: '...', token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in: 900, refresh_token: '...', refresh_url: '/auth/refresh', user: { email: 'demo1@ivy.homes' } }

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Tokens are stateless JWTs and are not invalidated server-side. Subsequent requests with the token still return 200.
findings.how_found: Sent authenticated request after calling POST /auth/logout
findings.impact: Requires strict client-side destruction of tokens to secure sessions
evidence: POST /auth/logout -> HTTP 200: {"ok": true, "note": "tokens are stateless; discard them client side"}
Subsequent GET /v1/listings with logged-out token -> HTTP 200 OK (token remains valid)

findings.documented: There is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts { refresh_token: '...' }, returning a newly refreshed access_token and refresh_token valid for another 900 seconds.
findings.how_found: Discovered refresh_url field in the POST /auth/login response and tested refreshing an active token via POST /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: Allows client sessions to stay authenticated seamlessly beyond the 15-minute access token lifespan.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with { refresh_token: '...' } -> HTTP 200: { access_token: '...', token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in: 900, refresh_token: '...' }

findings.documented: Endpoints are accessible with only an API key scoped to your city.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings, /v1/rentals, and /v1/projects return 401 'missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first' if called without an Authorization: Bearer <token> header.
findings.how_found: Sent GET /v1/listings with X-API-Key but omitted Authorization header and received 401 error.
findings.impact: All data reading and scraping requires performing the user authentication flow first.
evidence: GET /v1/listings with X-API-Key -> HTTP 401: {"detail": "missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first"}
GET /v1/rentals with X-API-Key -> HTTP 401: {"detail": "missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first"}
GET /v1/projects with X-API-Key -> HTTP 401: {"detail": "missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first"}

findings.documented: takes page and limit (default 20, max 200). Response: { total, page, page_size, results }
findings.actual: Ignores page, uses offset. Hard-caps limit at 50. Response envelope lacks page and page_size.
findings.how_found: Tested pagination limits and inspected response keys
findings.impact: Breaks standard page-based fetching logic
evidence: GET /v1/listings?page=2 -> returns offset: 0 and page 1 items
Response envelope: { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results } without page or page_size

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters. To fetch every record, read total, divide by your limit, and request that many pages.
findings.actual: Response total is severely underreported: listings reports total: 4917 but has 5100 retrievable records; rentals reports 2025 but has 2100; projects reports 569 but has 590.
findings.how_found: Iterated with offset until has_more was false, retrieving 5,100 listings, 2,100 rentals, and 590 projects instead of reported totals.
findings.impact: Applications terminating pagination based on reported total miss hundreds of valid listings, rentals, and projects.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns inactive listings as well; 1,083 out of 5,100 listings have is_live: false, which was not documented.
findings.how_found: Inspected response objects across all 5,100 listings and discovered the is_live boolean property with 1,083 false values.
findings.impact: Frontend must explicitly filter is_live === true to avoid displaying off-market or withdrawn properties to users.

findings.documented: Listing object schema defines 27 fields and promises inactive listings are excluded server-side.
findings.actual: Payload returned contains 28 fields; undocumented boolean is_live exists on all 5,100 records.
findings.how_found: Programmatic schema comparison between API_REFERENCE.md Listing schema and listings.json payload keys.
findings.impact: Strict schema validators reject responses due to unrecognized is_live field.

findings.documented: Supports min_price (int, inclusive), max_price (int, inclusive), and furnishing query parameters.
findings.actual: min_price, max_price, and furnishing query parameters are accepted by the server but silently ignored; response returns all listings regardless of criteria.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?furnishing=fully-furnished&min_price=10000000&max_price=15000000 and observed unfurnished properties and out-of-range prices returned.
findings.impact: Price range and furnishing filtering cannot be performed server-side and must be executed in client-side state.
evidence: GET /v1/listings?min_price=50000000 returns listings priced below 50M (e.g. 100-5000001 at 35.8M)

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: The project_id query parameter is silently ignored on /v1/listings, returning all city listings instead of filtering to the requested project.
findings.how_found: Called /v1/listings?project_id=P50001 and received total: 4917 with non-matching and null project IDs.
findings.impact: Filtering listings by builder project must be performed client-side.

findings.documented: order parameter accepts 'asc' or 'desc' for sort ordering.
findings.actual: order=desc is silently ignored by the server, always returning records in ascending order.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?sort_by=price&order=desc and compared with sort_by=price&order=asc; both returned identical ascending order.
findings.impact: Frontend sorting in descending order fails without client-side override.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} - A single listing.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found at singular /v1/listing/{id}. The active endpoint is plural: GET /v1/listings/{id}.
findings.how_found: Tested GET /v1/listing/MAG-5002240 (404) and GET /v1/listings/MAG-5002240 (200).
findings.impact: Detail view requests fail unless routing to the plural /v1/listings/{id}.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found on both singular and plural paths; endpoint was never implemented on the server.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings/MAG-5002240/similar and /v1/listing/MAG-5002240/similar with valid authentication.
findings.impact: Similar listing recommendations must be computed client-side.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body { id: '...' }, DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found. The active endpoints are GET /v1/saved, POST /v1/saved with body { listing_id: '...' }, and DELETE /v1/saved/{id}.
findings.how_found: Tested British and American spellings; discovered /v1/saved is the functional endpoint.
findings.impact: Favourites functionality fails completely unless using /v1/saved with listing_id payload key.

findings.documented: Endpoint is documented under the name /v1/favourites taking { id: '...' }.
findings.actual: POST /v1/saved requires JSON body { listing_id: '...' }. Passing { id: '...' } returns HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
findings.how_found: Sent POST /v1/saved with { id: ... } and received 422 validation error indicating 'listing_id' is required.
findings.impact: Saving listings requires conforming to the undocumented { listing_id } payload schema.
evidence: POST /v1/saved with body {"id": "MAG-5002240"} -> HTTP 422: Field required (body.listing_id)

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found on /v1/analytics/summary and /v1/analytics. No city analytics endpoint is implemented on the server.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/analytics/summary and related variations with valid auth; all returned 404.
findings.impact: Insights and dashboard screens must calculate market aggregates directly from listings and rental data.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees integer (Conventions: 'Money: Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API').
findings.actual: Project price_min and price_max are floating point values where numbers < 20 represent Crores (e.g. 12.44 Cr = 124,400,000 INR) and numbers >= 20 represent Lakhs (e.g. 90.8 L = 9,080,000 INR), never raw INR.
findings.how_found: Inspected project price values (ranging from 0.85 to 90.8) and compared with actual unit listing prices in the same projects (e.g. P50016 max 12.44 vs listings at ~12.4 Cr, P50096 min 90.8 vs listings at ~90 L).
findings.impact: Project UI displays incorrect pricing (e.g. Rs 12.44 instead of Rs 12.44 Crore) unless properly converted to INR.

findings.documented: Conventions: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: For portal 'magichomes', 455 listings report carpet_area in square meters (< 300, e.g. 47, 107, 114, 146) rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Analyzed area distribution across all portals; found areas < 300 exclusively on magichomes matching 1 sq m = 10.7639 sq ft.
findings.impact: Price per sqft calculations and unit displays are heavily skewed unless square meters are converted to square feet.

findings.documented: Conventions: Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Returns server_time with +05:30 IST offset and Asia/Kolkata timezone instead of UTC Z suffix.
findings.how_found: GET request against /health inspecting server_time value with +05:30 offset.
findings.impact: Parsers expecting strict UTC Z suffix fail or calculate local time offsets incorrectly.

findings.documented: total_listings is the number of listings currently available in the project. It is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: total_listings disagrees with the actual number of active listings for 446 out of 590 projects.
findings.how_found: Counted active listings grouped by project_id and compared against project total_listings across all 590 projects.
findings.impact: Users see conflicting inventory numbers on project details versus listing search results.

findings.documented: Bad parameter returns HTTP 400; Error bodies are {"detail": "..."} (single string message).
findings.actual: Server returns HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity with detail as an Array of validation error objects (e.g. [{loc, msg, type, input}]).
findings.how_found: Live network probe querying GET /v1/listings?limit=abc and POST /v1/saved with invalid payload.
findings.impact: Client error handlers assuming detail is a string display [object Object] or crash upon error parsing.
evidence: GET /v1/listings?limit=abc -> HTTP 422: [{"loc": ["query", "limit"], "msg": "Input should be a valid integer", "type": "int_parsing"}]
GET /v1/listings?limit=-5 -> HTTP 422: [{"loc": ["query", "limit"], "msg": "Input should be greater than 0", "type": "greater_than"}]

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to exactly one physical property and is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: Contains 33 physically impossible records across three categories: (a) carpet_area exceeding super_built_up_area, (b) floor number exceeding total_floors, and (c) negative or zero prices.
findings.how_found: Ran comprehensive integrity validation on physical constraints across all 5,100 listings.
findings.impact: Displays corrupted or physically impossible real estate records to users and corrupts statistical models.

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to exactly one physical property and is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: Contains 11 records with swapped latitude and longitude coordinates where latitude > 50 (~72.8° in Arctic Russia) and longitude < 50 (~19.0° in West Africa/Atlantic Ocean) instead of genuine Mumbai coordinates (lat ~19.0°, lon ~72.8°).
findings.how_found: Filtered all 5,100 listings for coordinate anomalies (latitude > 50 or longitude < 50) and identified inverted lat/lon pairs matching Mumbai's real coordinates in reverse.
findings.impact: Plotting properties on map interfaces places Mumbai homes in Arctic Siberia and the Atlantic Ocean.

findings.documented: Returns genuine active sale listings in your city.
findings.actual: Contains 11 fake listings with minuscule clickbait prices (< Rs 3,000/sqft in prime Mumbai localities) and syndicates of identical descriptions posted solely to attract leads and generate enquiries.
findings.how_found: Queried listings with anomalous price per sqft outliers and duplicate description clusters.
findings.impact: Deceives property buyers with unrealistic bait prices and corrupts price statistics.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Cross-portal duplicates exist where multiple portals list the same physical unit (same apartment, locality, floor, total floors, bedrooms, and facing). 5,100 records represent only 5,079 distinct physical properties.
findings.how_found: Deduplicated records using composite key of apartment name, locality, floor, total floors, bedroom count, and facing direction.
findings.impact: Buyers encounter duplicate listings of identical properties across different brokers and portals.

findings.documented: Collection returns active rental listings
findings.actual: Returns inactive rentals. 340 out of 2100 records contain undocumented is_live: false
findings.how_found: Audited /v1/rentals payloads
findings.impact: Users shown off-market rentals without client-side filtering

findings.documented: Supports sort_by and order desc
findings.actual: order=desc is silently ignored; returns ascending
findings.how_found: Compared desc and asc query results
findings.impact: Sorting UI fails server-side
